observations: Exactly one transparent outlined plate with a narrow thickness edge, not two plates. Horizontal incident and outgoing beams and a right-facing transmission observation reproduce the original apparatus.

The curved glyph and Turns around the beam label locate rotation at the plate without changing the beam direction. The approved context limits unchanged transmission under rotation to the ordinary unpolarized input; this is not a claim of no absorption.

The model's plate normal is along the beam and its crystal axis is transverse. The projected plate face and its mapped center match the candidate. No exact angle or intensity is printed in the figure.
Both 640 and 331 px previews are nonblank, readable, unclipped and free of label/geometry collisions. The plate outline, beam arrowheads, rotation glyph and observer remain distinguishable.
Monochrome semantic paint is a schematic, not a claim about green-light spectral conversion. English explanatory labels are deliberate additions to an unlabeled source apparatus.

independentSourceRequirementMap.verification: Axes / face view and identifiers 1/2 are visible, English and explicitly modern. Intermediate vector values are unprinted layout choices, not source measurements.

observations: The three ordered a/b/c rows each contain two plates and a right-side observer. The first plate has the same pose in every row; only the second plate changes orientation.

In a, the face-view crystal-axis keys are parallel and the outgoing beam is present. In b, key 1 remains vertical while key 2 is intermediate, the second plate carries the rotation glyph and the outgoing beam is visibly thinner with Dimmer text. In c, the keys are perpendicular and there is no outgoing beam, with No light out text.

The common physical face normals and transverse long-edge axes bind to the displayed projected vertices. The apparent change in projected second-plate shape is rotation within parallel transverse planes, not tilted surfaces, a rotated propagation axis or a switched first crystal axis.

All six plate faces are unfilled outlines with the same thickness-edge treatment; no separate opaque shutter or extra blocking object appears. Extinction occurs at the crossed second crystal while the incident/inter-plate beam and observer remain.
The face-view keys are explicitly labeled as a modern addition and are linked to plate identifiers 1/2. They do not add source apparatus or imply that the beam itself turns into a key axis.

Both 640 and 331 px previews preserve every row, axis key, plate identifier, intensity label and observer. The lower No light out label is clear of the plate, and the separated Axes / face view wording is readable without overlap.

The beam-width difference is qualitative and supplemented by English words, not a calibrated intensity fraction. The intermediate axis vector and congruent dimensions are declared layout regularization, not unprinted source measurements.
gateQualifications: The author's FIRST arrowhead export failures are technical failures. The retained repair-1 collision failure is separately preserved, and repair-2 is the one targeted label-layout repair, not an independent review retry.

The displayed apparatus is an oblique projection. The explicitly labeled face-view keys carry the aligned/intermediate/crossed transverse-axis comparison rather than relying on projected plate edges alone.
